newsitem.title: UK: Shell says received nine Brent Spar disposal bids.
newsitem.headline: Shell says received nine Brent Spar disposal bids.

text.p: The six international contractors selected to draw up detailed proposals for the disposal of the Brent Spar oil platform all submitted their bids by the June 2 deadline, Shell U.K. Exploration and Production (Shell Expro) said on Tuesday.
The engineering companies delivered bids covering nine of the original 11 shortlisted ideas, Shell Expro, the North Sea joint venture between Shell and Exxon said in a statement.
A high profile campaign by environmental group Greenpeace in 1995, which included a consumer boycott of Shell service stations, scuppered plans to dump the Brent Spar in the Atlantic Ocean.

One proposal to use parts of the Spar hull as a dock gate and one of the two proposals to use the top of the platform as an onshore training centre have been dropped by the contractors, the statement said.

"Now we've received the nine detailed bids, we can start the long process of comparing them with each other and with the benchmark option of deep sea disposal," said Eric Faulds, Shell Expro's Decommissioning Manager said.
Shell Expro has commissioned Norway's independent advisory body Det Norske Veritas (DNV) to review all the proposals, a process which will take around three months.
"There will then be further dialogue events before Shell makes a recommendation to the Department of Trade and Industry on the preferred way forward," the statement said.
Shell Expro must persuade the British government that the chosen alternative for Brent Spar, which has been parked in a Norwegian fjord since the Greenpeace campaign, is better than deep sea dumping.
The nine proposals include plans to use the platform as a fish farm development and as part of a coastal defence scheme for the east coast of England.
